task.description: REWORK REQUIRED. SS0's 'Verified precedents' section and SS4.3's mechanism both make a false claim about Letflow.EventStore.append/2's return shape: they state the persisted event's payload comes back as a JSON STRING that must be Jason.decode!/1'd to get a map. The validator traced this against real source and found it's wrong: Letflow.EventStore.Event's schema declares field(:payload, :map) (lib/letflow/event_store/event.ex:84, not :string), and EventStore.append/2's own insert_event/3 (lib/letflow/event_store.ex:607-641) sets the persisted row's payload to the ALREADY-DECODED map (Jason.decode!/1 already ran inside append/2 itself, at event_store.ex:239, for any inline-sized payload -- which an EXECUTION_ERROR event always is). interpret_transaction_result/1 (event_store.ex:697-707) returns {:ok, %{event: event, ...}} where event.payload is already a string-keyed map. Calling Jason.decode!/1 on it AGAIN (as SS4.3 currently instructs) is calling Jason.decode!/1 on a map(), which crashes at runtime -- Jason.decode/2 pattern-matches on a binary. Fix: (1) correct SS0's precedent bullet to accurately state event.payload is already a decoded map when read back from the Multi's changes (cite lib/letflow/event_store/event.ex:84 and lib/letflow/event_store.ex:607-641,697-707); (2) correct SS4.3's mechanism to read changes.execution_error_event.event.payload["reason"] directly off the map, with NO Jason.decode!/1 call anywhere in this path. Do not change anything else -- the orchestrator-absence finding, the land_service_task_exhaustion/2 design, the :execution_error_dlq_landing Multi step's positioning, the dlq_landed_externally opt threading, the last_failed_at/exhaustion-trigger resolutions, and both moduledoc deferred-follow-up sections all stand as validated.
